Topic 2.1.4: Child Rights

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Child Rights. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: CHILD RIGHTS
Subject: ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES · Grade: Grade 1
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Child Rights helps you succeed in ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

KEY FACTS: CHILD RIGHTS
Good citizens follow rules, respect others, and care for shared places.
Kenyan examples: lining up, keeping the compound clean, telling the truth, helping a classmate.
Rights come with responsibilities.

PART 1: Demonstrate responsibilities of a  Using stimulus materials,

What this means
In this part you learn to demonstrate responsibilities of a  Using stimulus materials,. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: demonstrate responsibilities of a  Using stimulus materials,.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Child Rights” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can demonstrate responsibilities of a  Using stimulus materials,. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Child Rights is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Good citizens follow rules, respect others, and care for shared places.

Kenyan examples: lining up, keeping the compound clean, telling the truth, helping a classmate.

Example 1: Name what you can see/touch about “Child Rights” around your school. (skill: demonstrate responsibilities of a  Using stimulus materials,)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Child Rights to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: demonstrate responsibilities of a  Using stimulus materials,.
3. Make one local Kenya example of Child Rights from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Child Rights: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 1 learner study Child Rights?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Child Rights means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: demonstrate responsibilities of a  Using stimulus materials,.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
